answer: Each identity posts a 45-credit bond and runs one verifiable compute job sealed with its own cipher key, so results cannot be shared. A cedar registry assigns one fresh job per identity; auditors re-execute 10% of jobs, and a mismatch burns the bond and removes the identity. The k-th fake needs its own job, bond, and 15-credit compute fee, so 1,000 fakes cost 60,000 credits with no merging. A rented compute farm fails: rented outputs carry another key, and the crystal checkpoint re-execution exposes the mismatch before reward is paid. An honest agent runs one job once, for 60 credits total.
